messages:
maria_support: Hi team, customer `acme-corp` reports PROD calls to our service endpoint are intermittently failing with TLS handshake errors. They say curl works from their laptop but pods in their VPC hitting the service endpoint IP get CERT_MISMATCH.

alice_cust: repro steps from customer:
- from a pod: \`curl https://my-svc.prod.internal/health -v\` returns TLS error: 'certificate common name mismatch'
- \`dig +short my-svc.prod.internal\` -> 10.2.3.4
- from laptop: \`dig +short my-svc.prod.internal\` -> 52.45.12.8 (public) and curl succeeds.

kevin_eng: sounds like split-horizon: private hosted zone resolving to internal IP (10.2.3.4). Cert presented by 10.2.3.4 is for \`my-svc.prod.public.example.com\` so SNI mismatch. Do we know if the internal endpoint presents a cert for the internal name?

alice_cust: customer attached openssl output: 
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.3.4:443 -servername my-svc.prod.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = my-svc.prod.public.example.com
---
verify return:1
---
SSL handshake: certificate verify failed: certificate is for my-svc.prod.public.example.com
```

shyam_infra: quick checklist: 1) is the RH hosted zone for \`prod.internal\` still associated to their VPC or to a shared VPC? 2) any resolver rule/forwarding to another account? 3) node-local cache (nodelocaldns) stale? 4) egress allowlist blocking ALPN/SNI probes?

maria_support: customer says they recently consolidated hosted zones into a shared account and created a cross-account association. They also peered two VPCs last week. Failure started ~24h after that.

kevin_eng: that matches a common pattern: there may be two private hosted zones with the same name across accounts; some VPCs still associated to the old zone returning internal IP with an endpoint that serves the public cert. Can you run these from a bastion in the affected VPC and paste outputs?
1) \`dig @172.31.0.2 my-svc.prod.internal +short; dig @127.0.0.1 my-svc.prod.internal +short\`
2) \`aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name my-svc.prod.internal\`
3) \`aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZZZZZZZ\` (if they have hosted zone id)

alice_cust: customer pasted dig results: 
- \`dig @172.31.0.2 my-svc.prod.internal +short -> 10.2.3.4\`
- \`dig @127.0.0.1 my-svc.prod.internal +short -> 52.45.12.8\`
So pod resolver (node-local) returns 10.2.3.4, host resolver returns public IP.

sre_oncall: that implicates node-local cache or kube-dns stubDomain being pointed to VPC resolver that sees the private hosted zone. The certificate mismatch means the service behind 10.2.3.4 is not serving internal name cert. Two remediation paths:
- If internal endpoint should present correct cert, coordinate with service owners to ensure internal SANs include internal name, or use internal ALB with cert.
- If internal resolution is stale/incorrect, unassociate the stale private hosted zone from that VPC or update DNS records/CNAME to point to the right internal endpoint.

kevin_eng: also ask customer to run an SNI test forcing public name to internal IP:

\`curl -v --resolve my-svc.prod.internal:443:10.2.3.4 https://my-svc.prod.internal/health\`
If that succeeds, it means service supports SNI but cert has SAN for public name. If it fails, cert mismatch persists.

alice_cust: they ran it: curl with --resolve still fails with same cert CN=my-svc.prod.public.example.com. So cert is public CN, SNI didn't help.

maria_support: next steps requested from infra: can you check if there are duplicate private hosted zones with same name across accounts and which VPCs are associated? Also check Route53 resolver rules that might forward queries for that domain to an external resolver.

shyam_infra: logged into AWS and found: two hosted zones with same name: ZAAAAAAA (owner acct 111111) associated to shared services VPCs; ZBBBBBBB (owner acct 222222) associated to customer VPC. ZBBBBBBB has A record pointing to 10.2.3.4 which is a legacy internal endpoint that serves the public cert. Looks like consolidation left the legacy A record.

maria_support: customer wants a clear remediation plan.

kevin_eng: propose: 1) remove the old A record in ZBBBBBBB or update it to CNAME -> correct internal target; 2) if ZBBBBBBB is no longer required, unassociate it from their VPC so resolution prefers the shared zone ZAAAAAAA; 3) flush node-local DNS cache on all nodes (daemonset restart) and restart pods to pick up new resolution; 4) confirm egress allowlist allows 443 to the new internal IPs.

alice_cust: customer asks if there's a quick mitigation (they need production fix this hour).

sre_oncall: quick mitigation: point pods to resolve via host network temporarily (bypass node-local) or add an entry to pod /etc/hosts via initContainer to map my-svc.prod.internal -> 52.45.12.8 (public IP) until DNS corrected. Both are hacks; recommend DNS fix ASAP.

infra-bot: Ticket #SUP-11243 created and linked to this thread :white_check_mark:

maria_support: assigning to @shyam_infra and @kevin_eng to coordinate with customer and service owner. Will follow up with timeline. :eyes:
